subject: Multiple fill scales with seperate legends

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Multiple fill scales with seperate legends
parts:
I know I'm moving past the initial scope of ggplot2 with this, but if
anyone have some ideas for how to accomplish this (with hacks if
necessary) I would be grateful.

Im using ggplot2 and ggdendro to create transcriptomic-like heatmaps
for peptide-intensity data (http://dl.dropbox.com/u/2323585/
AA1251heat.png). What I would like to do (and have crudely attempted
in the supplied graph) is to create an additional panel between the
heatmap and the dendrogram, holding colour coded information about
some covariate. In a perfect world this should also be done
vertically.

The most natural way would be to use geom_tile() in order to ensure
allignment, but as the scale_fill() is already used in the heatmap-
panel I cannot use this scale for another variable with a new colour
scheme.

Is there any way to add additional scales of the same type, however
cumbersome it is (e.g. manually create a scale_fill2 function and
setting fill2 instead of fill in the geom_tile)...

The code used can be found here: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/2323585/ggHeat.R

Note it uses some hacks proprietary of baptiste to alter the aspect
ratios of the facets: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/2323585/ggplot%20grid%20mod.r

Thanks for the help in advance...

Thomas Pedersen

messages.subject: Re: Multiple fill scales with seperate legends
parts:
How about using grid with truly separate plots and then putting them together? Each individual plot can have it's own scale and legend if necessary. 

I've never much played with that so I'm not much help other than to point out that there's quite a lot of that sort of thing in the archives of this user group.  

Brandon

I like having a unified graph and relying on faceting for my needs,
but you may be right in that this requires seperate grid plots... I
would still be interested in hearing how one can achieve multiples of
the same scale though...

The function provided should work with any matrix with provided
column- and row names, so I saw no need to provide a dataset (also I
work with proprietary information :-).

Thanks for the reply

Thomas

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Multiple fill scales with seperate legends
parts:
> I like having a unified graph and relying on faceting for my needs,
> but you may be right in that this requires seperate grid plots... I
> would still be interested in hearing how one can achieve multiples of
> the same scale though...

You can't - and it's unlikely you ever will be able to in the same
graph. I'm not completely opposed to multiple scales (although I
think there's the potential to create an incredibly confusing graph),
but it's a huge amount of work for something with a fairly limited set
of uses.

Hadley
